# choosewise.education

> An independent education resource on AI in schools, built and edited by Johan Lindström — a Swedish education consultant with 28 years in the school system (10 as teacher, 7 as school leader, 11 in EdTech). The site offers a four-step decision framework (WISE), downloadable prompt packs by role and subject, curated infographic styles for Gemini Notebook, and interactive AI-or-human tests. Content is published in English and Swedish; the Swedish surface uses the parallel name RÄTT-modellen.

The site's thesis: schools usually don't need more AI tools — they need the judgment to choose the right tool at the right time. Material is written for principals, school administrators (skolchefer), and teachers, and aims to be practical, evidence-aware, and free of vendor hype.

## The WISE Framework for Education

- [The WISE Framework for Education (English)](https://choosewise.education/wise/): Four-step decision model — Weigh the learning goal, Inspect what the subject requires, Select the right tool, Evaluate the outcome — for choosing AI tools in school settings.
- [RÄTT-modellen (Swedish)](https://choosewise.education/sv/ratt/): Same framework, Swedish surface and language.

## Prompt Packs

Free downloadable PDFs of ready-to-use AI chat prompts, organized by role and subject. Indices:

- [All prompts — English](https://choosewise.education/prompts/)
- [Alla promptar — Svenska](https://choosewise.education/sv/promptar/)

Sample role-based packs: Teachers, Principals, School administrators, District administrators, Superintendents, Lead teachers, EdTech coaches, Education strategists, School counselors, School psychologists, School nurses, School librarians, Special education specialists/teachers, Student assistants, Career counselors, School caretakers, School catering staff, School IT managers, District IT managers.

Sample subject-based packs (compulsory + upper secondary): Art, Biology, Chemistry, Crafts, Cross-curricular work, Digital tools, Early numeracy, English, Geography, History, Home economics, Mathematics, Modern languages, Music, Outdoor education, Physical education, Physics, Preschool, Reception, Religious studies, Science, Social studies, Technology, Time management, Learning new skills, Research on learning, Megaprompts (#1, #2, #3).

## AI or human?

- [AI or human? — English](https://choosewise.education/ai-or-human/)
- [AI eller människa? — Svenska](https://choosewise.education/sv/ai-eller-manniska/)

Interactive tests where visitors check whether they can tell AI-generated text, images, and video apart from human-created content.

## Infographic Styles

- [Infographic styles (140) — English](https://choosewise.education/infographic-styles/)
- [Infografik-stilar (140) — Svenska](https://choosewise.education/sv/infografik-stilar/)

A curated catalogue of 140 visual styles (with prompts) for generating Gemini Notebook video overviews and slide decks.

## Visual Codes

- [50 visual codes for ChatGPT — English](https://choosewise.education/visual-codes/)

Fifty one-word, slash-prefixed prompts (such as /cutaway, /anatomy, /ghosted) that turn an uploaded photo into a teaching visual in ChatGPT. Sorted into eight categories; every code is demonstrated with a draggable before/after slider on the same photo, and the page explains how to make your own.

- [Visual codes for video — English](https://choosewise.education/visual-codes/video/)

One-word codes for AI video: send a start image with a code such as /timelapse, /xray or /lightshift and get a five-second clip. Codes with classroom value (science processes, change over time, film language for art class) and for everyday use, each shown as start image and finished clip with the exact prompt. Codes that failed in testing are listed with what went wrong, and clips with factual errors are marked as "spot the error" material.

- [Visual codes for studying — English](https://choosewise.education/visual-codes/study/)

Codes such as /cheatsheet, /quizmate or /flashcards that, typed into an AI chatbot with a topic and "Make it an image", return a study poster or a worksheet. 27 codes tested on photosynthesis, the French Revolution and the Pythagorean theorem. Part 1 holds the codes that make students practise (each needs one added sentence, shown on its card); Part 2 the posters to read, each with a way to make reading active. The page explains that the codes are not official commands but the model's average reading of the word, documents the factual errors and weak answer keys found in testing, and lists four codes that failed.

## Think + AI

- [Think + AI — English](https://choosewise.education/think/)

Free tools that help teachers of Grades 8–12 train students' thinking when AI makes answers cheap. AI does the preparation on the teacher's side; students do the thinking, mostly without a screen.

- [Thinking Moves — English](https://choosewise.education/thinking-moves/)

Twelve five-minute thinking tasks (such as Best explanation, Check the claim, Then what? and Think back) grouped into six clusters of thinking. A prompt builder turns a subject, topic and grade into a prompt for any AI tool; each move has two worked examples from different subjects and an evidence label (Strong, Promising or Framework) that rates research on teaching that kind of thinking regularly. A free PDF card deck includes a fill-in prompt for offline use.

- [Flawed Answer — English](https://choosewise.education/flawed-answer/)

A fifteen-minute task for Grades 8–12. The teacher uses any AI tool to write a confident answer about the lesson topic that contains exactly one error of reasoning, of one of six types (wrong cause, correlation as cause, missing step, overgeneralisation, hidden assumption, right answer for the wrong reason), at one of two difficulty levels. Students are told an AI wrote it and, in pairs, find the flaw, fix it, explain why it convinces and say how they would test it. Six worked examples with teacher keys, an upper-secondary variant, a one-page student frame and a PDF card deck.
